NKJV.1: “Give ear, O heavens, and I will speak; And hear, O earth, the words of my mouth.
NKJV.2: Let my teaching drop as the rain, My speech distill as the dew,  As raindrops on the tender herb, And as showers on the grass.
NKJV.3: For I proclaim the name of the LORD:  Ascribe greatness to our God.
NKJV.4: He is the Rock, His work is perfect; For all His ways are justice, A God of truth and without injustice; Righteous and upright is He.
NKJV.5: “They have corrupted themselves; They are not His children, Because of their blemish: A perverse and crooked generation.
NKJV.6: Do you thus deal with the LORD, O foolish and unwise people? Is He not your Father, who bought you? Has He not made you and established you?
NKJV.7: “Remember  the days of old, Consider the years of many generations.  Ask your father, and he will show you; Your elders, and they will tell you:
NKJV.8: When the Most High divided their inheritance to the nations, When He separated the sons of Adam, He set the boundaries of the peoples According to the number of the children of Israel.
NKJV.9: For the LORD’s portion is His people; Jacob is the place of His inheritance.
NKJV.10: “He found him in a desert land And in the wasteland, a howling wilderness; He encircled him, He instructed him, He kept him as the apple of His eye.
NKJV.11: As an eagle stirs up its nest, Hovers over its young, Spreading out its wings, taking them up, Carrying them on its wings,
NKJV.12: So the LORD alone led him, And there was no foreign god with him.
NKJV.13: “He  made him ride in the heights of the earth, That he might eat the produce of the fields; He made him draw honey from the rock, And oil from the flinty rock;
NKJV.14: Curds from the cattle, and milk of the flock,  With fat of lambs; And rams of the breed of Bashan, and goats, With the choicest wheat; And you drank wine, the blood of the grapes.
NKJV.15: “But Jeshurun grew fat and kicked; You grew fat, you grew thick, You are obese! Then he forsook God who made him, And scornfully esteemed the Rock of his salvation.
NKJV.16: They provoked Him to jealousy with foreign gods; With abominations they provoked Him to anger.
NKJV.17: They sacrificed to demons, not to God, To gods they did not know, To new gods, new arrivals That your fathers did not fear.
NKJV.18: Of the Rock who begot you, you are unmindful, And have forgotten the God who fathered you.
NKJV.19: “And when the LORD saw it, He spurned them, Because of the provocation of His sons and His daughters.
NKJV.20: And He said: ‘I will hide My face from them, I will see what their end will be, For they are a perverse generation, Children in whom is no faith.
NKJV.21: They have provoked Me to jealousy by what is not God; They have moved Me to anger by their foolish idols. But I will provoke them to jealousy by those who are not a nation; I will move them to anger by a foolish nation.
NKJV.22: For a fire is kindled in My anger, And shall burn to the lowest hell; It shall consume the earth with her increase, And set on fire the foundations of the mountains.
NKJV.23: ‘I will heap disasters on them;  I will spend My arrows on them.
NKJV.24: They shall be wasted with hunger, Devoured by pestilence and bitter destruction; I will also send against them the teeth of beasts, With the poison of serpents of the dust.
NKJV.25: The sword shall destroy outside; There shall be terror within For the young man and virgin, The nursing child with the man of gray hairs.
NKJV.26: I would have said, “I will dash them in pieces, I will make the memory of them to cease from among men,”
NKJV.27: Had I not feared the wrath of the enemy, Lest their adversaries should misunderstand, Lest they should say, “Our hand is high; And it is not the LORD who has done all this.” ’
NKJV.28: “For they are a nation void of counsel, Nor is there any understanding in them.
NKJV.29: Oh, that they were wise, that they understood this, That they would consider their latter end!
NKJV.30: How could one chase a thousand, And two put ten thousand to flight, Unless their Rock had sold them, And the LORD had surrendered them?
NKJV.31: For their rock is not like our Rock, Even our enemies themselves being judges.
NKJV.32: For their vine is of the vine of Sodom And of the fields of Gomorrah; Their grapes are grapes of gall, Their clusters are bitter.
NKJV.33: Their wine is the poison of serpents, And the cruel venom of cobras.
NKJV.34: ‘Is this not laid up in store with Me, Sealed up among My treasures?
NKJV.35: Vengeance is Mine, and recompense; Their foot shall slip in due time; For the day of their calamity is at hand, And the things to come hasten upon them.’
NKJV.36: “For the LORD will judge His people And have compassion on His servants, When He sees that their power is gone, And there is no one remaining, bond or free.
NKJV.37: He will say: ‘Where are their gods, The rock in which they sought refuge?
NKJV.38: Who ate the fat of their sacrifices, And drank the wine of their drink offering? Let them rise and help you, And be your refuge.
NKJV.39: ‘Now see that I, even I, am He, And there is no God besides Me; I kill and I make alive; I wound and I heal; Nor is there any who can deliver from My hand.
NKJV.40: For I raise My hand to heaven, And say, “As I live forever,
NKJV.41: If I whet My glittering sword, And My hand takes hold on judgment, I will render vengeance to My enemies, And repay those who hate Me.
NKJV.42: I will make My arrows drunk with blood, And My sword shall devour flesh, With the blood of the slain and the captives, From the heads of the leaders of the enemy.” ’
NKJV.43: “Rejoice, O Gentiles, with His people; For He will avenge the blood of His servants, And render vengeance to His adversaries; He will provide atonement for His land and His people.”
NKJV.44: So Moses came with Joshua the son of Nun and spoke all the words of this song in the hearing of the people.
NKJV.45: Moses finished speaking all these words to all Israel,
NKJV.46: and he said to them: “Set your hearts on all the words which I testify among you today, which you shall command your children to be careful to observe—all the words of this law.
NKJV.47: For it is not a futile thing for you, because it is your life, and by this word you shall prolong your days in the land which you cross over the Jordan to possess.”
NKJV.48: Then the LORD spoke to Moses that very same day, saying:
NKJV.49: “Go up this mountain of the Abarim, Mount Nebo, which is in the land of Moab, across from Jericho; view the land of Canaan, which I give to the children of Israel as a possession;
NKJV.50: and die on the mountain which you ascend, and be gathered to your people, just as Aaron your brother died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people;
NKJV.51: because you trespassed against Me among the children of Israel at the waters of Meribah Kadesh, in the Wilderness of Zin, because you did not hallow Me in the midst of the children of Israel.
NKJV.52: Yet you shall see the land before you, though you shall not go there, into the land which I am giving to the children of Israel.”

NASB.1: 'Give ear, O heavens, and let me speak; And let the earth hear the words of my mouth.
NASB.2: 'Let my teaching drop as the rain, My speech distill as the dew, As the droplets on the fresh grass And as the showers on the herb.
NASB.3: 'For I proclaim the name of the LORD; Ascribe greatness to our God!
NASB.4: 'The Rock! His work is perfect, For all His ways are just; A God of faithfulness and without injustice, Righteous and upright is He.
NASB.5: 'They have acted corruptly toward Him, [They are] not His children, because of their defect; [But are] a perverse and crooked generation.
NASB.6: 'Do you thus repay the LORD, O foolish and unwise people? Is not He your Father who has bought you? He has made you and established you.
NASB.7: 'Remember the days of old, Consider the years of all generations. Ask your father, and he will inform you, Your elders, and they will tell you.
NASB.8: 'When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance, When He separated the sons of man, He set the boundaries of the peoples According to the number of the sons of Israel.
NASB.9: 'For the LORD'S portion is His people; Jacob is the allotment of His inheritance.
NASB.10: 'He found him in a desert land, And in the howling waste of a wilderness; He encircled him, He cared for him, He guarded him as the pupil of His eye.
NASB.11: 'Like an eagle that stirs up its nest, That hovers over its young, He spread His wings and caught them, He carried them on His pinions.
NASB.12: 'The LORD alone guided him, And there was no foreign god with him.
NASB.13: 'He made him ride on the high places of the earth, And he ate the produce of the field; And He made him suck honey from the rock, And oil from the flinty rock,
NASB.14: Curds of cows, and milk of the flock, With fat of lambs, And rams, the breed of Bashan, and goats, With the finest of the wheat-- And of the blood of grapes you drank wine.
NASB.15: 'But Jeshurun grew fat and kicked-- You are grown fat, thick, and sleek-- Then he forsook God who made him, And scorned the Rock of his salvation.
NASB.16: 'They made Him jealous with strange [gods]; With abominations they provoked Him to anger.
NASB.17: 'They sacrificed to demons who were not God, To gods whom they have not known, New [gods] who came lately, Whom your fathers did not dread.
NASB.18: 'You neglected the Rock who begot you, And forgot the God who gave you birth.
NASB.19: 'The LORD saw [this], and spurned [them] Because of the provocation of His sons and daughters.
NASB.20: 'Then He said, 'I will hide My face from them, I will see what their end [shall be]; For they are a perverse generation, Sons in whom is no faithfulness.
NASB.21: 'They have made Me jealous with [what] is not God; They have provoked Me to anger with their idols. So I will make them jealous with [those who] are not a people; I will provoke them to anger with a foolish nation,
NASB.22: For a fire is kindled in My anger, And burns to the lowest part of Sheol, And consumes the earth with its yield, And sets on fire the foundations of the mountains.
NASB.23: 'I will heap misfortunes on them; I will use My arrows on them.
NASB.24: '[They will be] wasted by famine, and consumed by plague And bitter destruction; And the teeth of beasts I will send upon them, With the venom of crawling things of the dust.
NASB.25: 'Outside the sword will bereave, And inside terror-- Both young man and virgin, The nursling with the man of gray hair.
NASB.26: 'I would have said, 'I will cut them to pieces, I will remove the memory of them from men,'
NASB.27: Had I not feared the provocation by the enemy, That their adversaries would misjudge, That they would say, 'Our hand is triumphant, And the LORD has not done all this.''
NASB.28: 'For they are a nation lacking in counsel, And there is no understanding in them.
NASB.29: 'Would that they were wise, that they understood this, That they would discern their future!
NASB.30: 'How could one chase a thousand, And two put ten thousand to flight, Unless their Rock had sold them, And the LORD had given them up?
NASB.31: 'Indeed their rock is not like our Rock, Even our enemies themselves judge this.
NASB.32: 'For their vine is from the vine of Sodom, And from the fields of Gomorrah; Their grapes are grapes of poison, Their clusters, bitter.
NASB.33: 'Their wine is the venom of serpents, And the deadly poison of cobras.
NASB.34: 'Is it not laid up in store with Me, Sealed up in My treasuries?
NASB.35: 'Vengeance is Mine, and retribution, In due time their foot will slip; For the day of their calamity is near, And the impending things are hastening upon them.'
NASB.36: 'For the LORD will vindicate His people, And will have compassion on His servants, When He sees that [their] strength is gone, And there is none [remaining], bond or free.
NASB.37: 'And He will say, 'Where are their gods, The rock in which they sought refuge?
NASB.38: 'Who ate the fat of their sacrifices, [And] drank the wine of their drink offering? Let them rise up and help you, Let them be your hiding place!
NASB.39: 'See now that I, I am He, And there is no god besides Me; It is I who put to death and give life. I have wounded and it is I who heal, And there is no one who can deliver from My hand.
NASB.40: 'Indeed, I lift up My hand to heaven, And say, as I live forever,
NASB.41: If I sharpen My flashing sword, And My hand takes hold on justice, I will render vengeance on My adversaries, And I will repay those who hate Me.
NASB.42: 'I will make My arrows drunk with blood, And My sword will devour flesh, With the blood of the slain and the captives, From the long-haired leaders of the enemy.'
NASB.43: 'Rejoice, O nations, [with] His people; For He will avenge the blood of His servants, And will render vengeance on His adversaries, And will atone for His land [and] His people.'
NASB.44: Then Moses came and spoke all the words of this song in the hearing of the people, he, with Joshua the son of Nun.
NASB.45: When Moses had finished speaking all these words to all Israel,
NASB.46: he said to them, 'Take to your heart all the words with which I am warning you today, which you shall command your sons to observe carefully, [even] all the words of this law.
NASB.47: 'For it is not an idle word for you; indeed it is your life. And by this word you will prolong your days in the land, which you are about to cross the Jordan to possess.'
NASB.48: The LORD spoke to Moses that very same day, saying,
NASB.49: 'Go up to this mountain of the Abarim, Mount Nebo, which is in the land of Moab opposite Jericho, and look at the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the sons of Israel for a possession.
NASB.50: 'Then die on the mountain where you ascend, and be gathered to your people, as Aaron your brother died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people,
NASB.51: because you broke faith with Me in the midst of the sons of Israel at the waters of Meribah-kadesh, in the wilderness of Zin, because you did not treat Me as holy in the midst of the sons of Israel.
NASB.52: 'For you shall see the land at a distance, but you shall not go there, into the land which I am giving the sons of Israel.'

WEB.41: if I sharpen my glittering sword, my hand grasps it in judgment; I will take vengeance on my adversaries, and will repay those who hate me.
WEB.42: I will make my arrows drunk with blood. My sword shall devour flesh with the blood of the slain and the captives, from the head of the leaders of the enemy.”

NLT.1:

NLT.2:

like gentle showers on young plants.
NLT.3:
I will proclaim the name of the LORD;
how glorious is our God!
NLT.4:
He is the Rock; his deeds are perfect.
Everything he does is just and fair.
He is a faithful God who does no wrong;
how just and upright he is!
NLT.5:
“But they have acted corruptly toward him;
when they act so perversely,
are they really his children?
They are a deceitful and twisted generation.
NLT.6:
Is this the way you repay the LORD,
you foolish and senseless people?
Isn’t he your Father who created you?
Has he not made you and established you?
NLT.7:
Remember the days of long ago;
think about the generations past.
Ask your father, and he will inform you.
Inquire of your elders, and they will tell you.
NLT.8:
When the Most High assigned lands to the nations,
when he divided up the human race,
he established the boundaries of the peoples
according to the number in his heavenly court.
NLT.9:
“For the people of Israel belong to the LORD;
Jacob is his special possession.
NLT.10:
He found them in a desert land,
in an empty, howling wasteland.
He surrounded them and watched over them;
he guarded them as he would guard his own eyes.
NLT.11:
Like an eagle that rouses her chicks
and hovers over her young,
so he spread his wings to take them up
and carried them safely on his pinions.
NLT.12:
The LORD alone guided them;
they followed no foreign gods.
NLT.13:
He let them ride over the highlands
and feast on the crops of the fields.
He nourished them with honey from the rock
and olive oil from the stony ground.
NLT.14:
He fed them yogurt from the herd
and milk from the flock,
together with the fat of lambs.
He gave them choice rams from Bashan, and goats,
together with the choicest wheat.
You drank the finest wine,
made from the juice of grapes.
NLT.15:
“But Israel soon became fat and unruly;
the people grew heavy, plump, and stuffed!
Then they abandoned the God who had made them;
they made light of the Rock of their salvation.
NLT.16:
They stirred up his jealousy by worshiping foreign gods;
they provoked his fury with detestable deeds.
NLT.17:
They offered sacrifices to demons, which are not God,
to gods they had not known before,
to new gods only recently arrived,
to gods their ancestors had never feared.
NLT.18:
You neglected the Rock who had fathered you;
you forgot the God who had given you birth.
NLT.19:
“The LORD saw this and drew back,
provoked to anger by his own sons and daughters.
NLT.20:
He said, ‘I will abandon them;
then see what becomes of them.
For they are a twisted generation,
children without integrity.
NLT.21:
They have roused my jealousy by worshiping things that are not God;
they have provoked my anger with their useless idols.
Now I will rouse their jealousy through people who are not even a people;
I will provoke their anger through the foolish Gentiles.
NLT.22:
For my anger blazes forth like fire
and burns to the depths of the grave.
It devours the earth and all its crops
and ignites the foundations of the mountains.
NLT.23:
I will heap disasters upon them
and shoot them down with my arrows.
NLT.24:
I will weaken them with famine,
burning fever, and deadly disease.
I will send the fangs of wild beasts
and poisonous snakes that glide in the dust.
NLT.25:
Outside, the sword will bring death,
and inside, terror will strike
both young men and young women,
both infants and the aged.
NLT.26:
I would have annihilated them,
wiping out even the memory of them.
NLT.27:
But I feared the taunt of Israel’s enemy,
who might misunderstand and say,
“Our own power has triumphed!
The LORD had nothing to do with this!”’
NLT.28:
“But Israel is a senseless nation;
the people are foolish, without understanding.
NLT.29:
Oh, that they were wise and could understand this!
Oh, that they might know their fate!
NLT.30:
How could one person chase a thousand of them,
and two people put ten thousand to flight,
unless their Rock had sold them,
unless the LORD had given them up?
NLT.31:
But the rock of our enemies is not like our Rock,
as even they recognize.
NLT.32:
Their vine grows from the vine of Sodom,
from the vineyards of Gomorrah.
Their grapes are poison,
and their clusters are bitter.
NLT.33:
Their wine is the venom of serpents,
the deadly poison of cobras.
NLT.34:
“The LORD says, ‘Am I not storing up these things,
sealing them away in my treasury?
NLT.35:
I will take revenge; I will pay them back.
In due time their feet will slip.
Their day of disaster will arrive,
and their destiny will overtake them.’
NLT.36:
“Indeed, the LORD will give justice to his people,
and he will change his mind about his servants,
when he sees their strength is gone
and no one is left, slave or free.
NLT.37:
Then he will ask, ‘Where are their gods,
the rocks they fled to for refuge?
NLT.38:
Where now are those gods,
who ate the fat of their sacrifices
and drank the wine of their offerings?
Let those gods arise and help you!
Let them provide you with shelter!
NLT.39:
Look now; I myself am he!
There is no other god but me!
I am the one who kills and gives life;
I am the one who wounds and heals;
no one can be rescued from my powerful hand!
NLT.40:
Now I raise my hand to heaven
and declare, “As surely as I live,
NLT.41:
when I sharpen my flashing sword
and begin to carry out justice,
I will take revenge on my enemies
and repay those who reject me.
NLT.42:
I will make my arrows drunk with blood,
and my sword will devour flesh —
the blood of the slaughtered and the captives,
and the heads of the enemy leaders.”’
NLT.43:
“Rejoice with him, you heavens,
and let all of God’s angels worship him.
Rejoice with his people, you Gentiles,
and let all the angels be strengthened in him.
For he will avenge the blood of his children ;
he will take revenge against his enemies.
He will repay those who hate him
and cleanse his people’s land.”
NLT.44: So Moses came with Joshua son of Nun and recited all the words of this song to the people.
NLT.45: When Moses had finished reciting all these words to the people of Israel,
NLT.46: he added: “Take to heart all the words of warning I have given you today. Pass them on as a command to your children so they will obey every word of these instructions.

NLT.49: “Go to Moab, to the mountains east of the river, and climb Mount Nebo, which is across from Jericho. Look out across the land of Canaan, the land I am giving to the people of Israel as their own special possession.

NLT.51: For both of you betrayed me with the Israelites at the waters of Meribah at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin. You failed to demonstrate my holiness to the people of Israel there.
NLT.52: So you will see the land from a distance, but you may not enter the land I am giving to the people of Israel.”

Their vine comes from the vinestock of Sodom,

their grapes are grapes of poison,
their clusters are bitter;
NRSVCE.33:
their wine is the poison of serpents,
the cruel venom of asps.
NRSVCE.34:
Is not this laid up in store with me,
sealed up in my treasuries?
NRSVCE.35:
Vengeance is mine, and recompense,

because the day of their calamity is at hand,
their doom comes swiftly.
NRSVCE.36:
Indeed the LORD will vindicate his people,
have compassion on his servants,
when he sees that their power is gone,
neither bond nor free remaining.

Then he will say: Where are their gods,

NRSVCE.38:
who ate the fat of their sacrifices,

NRSVCE.39:
See now that I, even I, am he;

NRSVCE.40:
For I lift up my hand to heaven,

when I whet my flashing sword,

NRSVCE.42:

MSG.1:
Listen, Heavens, I have something to tell you.
Attention, Earth, I've got a mouth full of words.
MSG.2:
My teaching, let it fall like a gentle rain,
my words arrive like morning dew,
Like a sprinkling rain on new grass,
like spring showers on the garden.
MSG.3:
For it's God's Name I'm preaching—
respond to the greatness of our God!
MSG.4:
The Rock: His works are perfect,
and the way he works is fair and just;
A God you can depend upon, no exceptions,
a straight-arrow God.
MSG.5:
His messed-up, mixed-up children, his non-children,
throw mud at him but none of it sticks.
MSG.6:
Don't you realize it is God you are treating like this?
This is crazy; don't you have any sense of reverence?
Isn't this your father who created you,
who made you and gave you a place on Earth?
MSG.7:
Read up on what happened before you were born;
dig into the past, understand your roots.
Ask your parents what it was like before you were born;
ask the old-ones, they'll tell you a thing or two.
MSG.8:
When the High God gave the nations their stake,
gave them their place on Earth,
He put each of the peoples within boundaries
under the care of divine guardians.
MSG.9:
But God himself took charge of his people,
took Jacob on as his personal concern.
MSG.10:
He found him out in the wilderness,
in an empty, windswept wasteland.
He threw his arms around him, lavished attention on him,
guarding him as the apple of his eye.
MSG.11:
He was like an eagle hovering over its nest,
overshadowing its young,
Then spreading its wings, lifting them into the air,
teaching them to fly.
MSG.12:
God alone led him;
there was not a foreign god in sight.
MSG.13:
God lifted him on to the hilltops,
so he could feast on the crops in the fields.
He fed him honey from the rock,
oil from granite crags,
MSG.14:
Curds of cattle and the milk of sheep,
the choice cuts of lambs and goats,
Fine Bashan rams, high-quality wheat,
and the blood of grapes: you drank good wine!
MSG.15:
Jeshurun put on weight and bucked;
you got fat, became obese, a tub of lard.
He abandoned the God who made him,
he mocked the Rock of his salvation.
MSG.16:
They made him jealous with their foreign newfangled gods,
and with obscenities they vexed him no end.
MSG.17:
They sacrificed to no-god demons,
gods they knew nothing about,
The latest in gods, fresh from the market,
gods your ancestors would never call "gods."
MSG.18:
You walked out on the Rock who gave you your life,
forgot the birth-God who brought you into the world.
MSG.19:
God saw it and turned on his heel,
angered and hurt by his sons and daughters.
MSG.20:
He said, "From now on I'm looking the other way.
Wait and see what happens to them.
Oh, they're a turned-around, upside-down generation!
Who knows what they'll do from one moment to the next?
MSG.21:
They've goaded me with their no-gods,
infuriated me with their hot-air gods;
I'm going to goad them with a no-people,
with a hollow nation incense them.
MSG.22:
My anger started a fire,
a wildfire burning deep down in Sheol,
Then shooting up and devouring the Earth and its crops,
setting all the mountains, from bottom to top, on fire.
MSG.23:
I'll pile catastrophes on them,
I'll shoot my arrows at them:
MSG.24:
Starvation, blistering heat, killing disease;
I'll send snarling wild animals to attack from the forest
and venomous creatures to strike from the dust.
MSG.25:
Killing in the streets,
terror in the houses,
Young men and virgins alike struck down,
and yes, breast-feeding babies and gray-haired old men."
MSG.26:
I could have said, "I'll hack them to pieces,
wipe out all trace of them from the Earth,"
MSG.27:
Except that I feared the enemy would grab the chance
to take credit for all of it,
Crowing, "Look what we did!
God had nothing to do with this."
MSG.28:
They are a nation of ninnies,
they don't know enough to come in out of the rain.
MSG.29:
If they had any sense at all, they'd know this;
they would see what's coming down the road.
MSG.30:
How could one soldier chase a thousand enemies off,
or two men run off two thousand,
Unless their Rock had sold them,
unless God had given them away?
MSG.31:
For their rock is nothing compared to our Rock;
even our enemies say that.
MSG.32:
They're a vine that comes right out of Sodom,
who they are is rooted in Gomorrah;
Their grapes are poison grapes,
their grape-clusters bitter.
MSG.33:
Their wine is rattlesnake venom,
mixed with lethal cobra poison.
MSG.34:
Don't you realize that I have my shelves
well stocked, locked behind iron doors?
MSG.35:
I'm in charge of vengeance and payback,
just waiting for them to slip up;
And the day of their doom is just around the corner,
sudden and swift and sure.
MSG.36:
Yes, God will judge his people,
but oh how compassionately he'll do it.
When he sees their weakened plight
and there is no one left, slave or free,
MSG.37:
He'll say, "So where are their gods,
the rock in which they sought refuge,
MSG.38:
The gods who feasted on the fat of their sacrifices
and drank the wine of their drink-offerings?
Let them show their stuff and help you,
let them give you a hand!
MSG.39:
"Do you see it now? Do you see that I'm the one?
Do you see that there's no other god beside me?
I bring death and I give life, I wound and I heal—
there is no getting away from or around me!
MSG.40:
I raise my hand in solemn oath;
I say, 'I'm always around. By that very life I promise:
MSG.41:
When I sharpen my lightning sword
and execute judgment,
I take vengeance on my enemies
and pay back those who hate me.
MSG.42:
I'll make my arrows drunk with blood,
my sword will gorge itself on flesh,
Feasting on slain and captive alike,
the proud and vain enemy corpses.' "
MSG.43:
Celebrate, nations, join the praise of his people.
He avenges the deaths of his servants,
Pays back his enemies with vengeance,
and cleanses his land for his people.
MSG.44: Moses came and recited all the words of this song in the hearing of the people, he and Joshua son of Nun.
MSG.45: When Moses had finished saying all these words to all Israel,
MSG.46: he said, "Take to heart all these words to which I give witness today and urgently command your children to put them into practice, every single word of this Revelation.
MSG.47: Yes. This is no small matter for you; it's your life. In keeping this word you'll have a good and long life in this land that you're crossing the Jordan to possess."
MSG.48: That same day God spoke to Moses:
MSG.49: "Climb the Abarim Mountains to Mount Nebo in the land of Moab, overlooking Jericho, and view the land of Canaan that I'm giving the People of Israel to have and hold.
MSG.50: Die on the mountain that you climb and join your people in the ground, just as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and joined his people.
MSG.51: "This is because you broke faith with me in the company of the People of Israel at the Waters of Meribah Kadesh in the Wilderness of Zin—you didn't honor my Holy Presence in the company of the People of Israel.
MSG.52: You'll look at the land spread out before you but you won't enter it, this land that I am giving to the People of Israel."

NET.1: Listen, O heavens, and I will speak; hear, O earth, the words of my mouth.
NET.2: My teaching will drop like the rain, my sayings will drip like the dew, as rain drops upon the grass, and showers upon new growth.
NET.3: For I will proclaim the name of the LORD; you must acknowledge the greatness of our God.
NET.4: As for the Rock, his work is perfect, for all his ways are just. He is a reliable God who is never unjust, he is fair and upright.
NET.5: His people have been unfaithful to him; they have not acted like his children — this is their sin. They are a perverse and deceitful generation.
NET.6: Is this how you repay the LORD, you foolish, unwise people? Is he not your father, your creator? He has made you and established you.
NET.7: Remember the ancient days; bear in mind the years of past generations. Ask your father and he will inform you, your elders, and they will tell you.
NET.8: When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance, when he divided up humankind, he set the boundaries of the peoples, according to the number of the heavenly assembly.
NET.9: For the LORD’s allotment is his people, Jacob is his special possession.
NET.10: The LORD found him in a desolate land, in an empty wasteland where animals howl. He continually guarded him and taught him; he continually protected him like the pupil of his eye.
NET.11: Like an eagle that stirs up its nest, that hovers over its young, so the LORD spread out his wings and took him, he lifted him up on his pinions.
NET.12: The LORD alone was guiding him, no foreign god was with him.
NET.13: He enabled him to travel over the high terrain of the land, and he ate of the produce of the fields. He provided honey for him from the cliffs, and olive oil from the hardest of rocks,
NET.14: butter from the herd and milk from the flock, along with the fat of lambs, rams and goats of Bashan, along with the best of the kernels of wheat; and from the juice of grapes you drank wine.
NET.15: But Jeshurun became fat and kicked, you got fat, thick, and stuffed! Then he deserted the God who made him, and treated the Rock who saved him with contempt.
NET.16: They made him jealous with other gods, they enraged him with abhorrent idols.
NET.17: They sacrificed to demons, not God, to gods they had not known; to new gods who had recently come along, gods your ancestors had not known about.
NET.18: You have forgotten the Rock who fathered you, and put out of mind the God who gave you birth.
NET.19: But the LORD took note and despised them because his sons and daughters enraged him.
NET.20: He said, “I will reject them, I will see what will happen to them; for they are a perverse generation, children who show no loyalty.
NET.21: They have made me jealous with false gods, enraging me with their worthless gods; so I will make them jealous with a people they do not recognize, with a nation slow to learn I will enrage them.
NET.22: For a fire has been kindled by my anger, and it burns to lowest Sheol; it consumes the earth and its produce, and ignites the foundations of the mountains.
NET.23: I will increase their disasters, I will use up my arrows on them.
NET.24: They will be starved by famine, eaten by plague, and bitterly stung; I will send the teeth of wild animals against them, along with the poison of creatures that crawl in the dust.
NET.25: The sword will make people childless outside, and terror will do so inside; they will destroy both the young man and the virgin, the infant and the gray-haired man.
NET.26: “I said, ‘I want to cut them in pieces. I want to make people forget they ever existed.
NET.27: But I fear the reaction of their enemies, for their adversaries would misunderstand and say, “Our power is great, and the LORD has not done all this!”’
NET.28: They are a nation devoid of wisdom, and there is no understanding among them.
NET.29: I wish that they were wise and could understand this, and that they could comprehend what will happen to them.”
NET.30: How can one man chase a thousand of them, and two pursue ten thousand; unless their Rock had delivered them up, and the LORD had handed them over?
NET.31: For our enemies’ rock is not like our Rock, as even our enemies concede.
NET.32: For their vine is from the stock of Sodom, and from the fields of Gomorrah. Their grapes contain venom, their clusters of grapes are bitter.
NET.33: Their wine is snakes’ poison, the deadly venom of cobras.
NET.34: “Is this not stored up with me?” says the LORD, “Is it not sealed up in my storehouses?
NET.35: I will get revenge and pay them back at the time their foot slips; for the day of their disaster is near, and the impending judgment is rushing upon them!”
NET.36: The LORD will judge his people, and will change his plans concerning his servants; when he sees that their power has disappeared, and that no one is left, whether confined or set free.
NET.37: He will say, “Where are their gods, the rock in whom they sought security,
NET.38: who ate the best of their sacrifices, and drank the wine of their drink offerings? Let them rise and help you; let them be your refuge!
NET.39: “See now that I, indeed I, am he!” says the LORD, “and there is no other god besides me. I kill and give life, I smash and I heal, and none can resist my power.
NET.40: For I raise up my hand to heaven, and say, ‘As surely as I live forever,
NET.41: I will sharpen my lightning-like sword, and my hand will grasp hold of the weapon of judgment; I will execute vengeance on my foes, and repay those who hate me!
NET.42: I will make my arrows drunk with blood, and my sword will devour flesh — the blood of the slaughtered and captured, the chief of the enemy’s leaders!’”
NET.43: Cry out, O nations, with his people, for he will avenge his servants’ blood; he will take vengeance against his enemies, and make atonement for his land and people.
NET.44: Then Moses went with Joshua son of Nun and recited all the words of this song to the people.
NET.45: When Moses finished reciting all these words to all Israel
NET.46: he said to them, “Keep in mind all the words I am solemnly proclaiming to you today; you must command your children to observe carefully all the words of this law.
NET.47: For this is no idle word for you — it is your life! By this word you will live a long time in the land you are about to cross the Jordan to possess.”
NET.48: Then the LORD said to Moses that same day,
NET.49: “Go up to this Abarim hill country, to Mount Nebo (which is in the land of Moab opposite Jericho ) and look at the land of Canaan that I am giving to the Israelites as a possession.
NET.50: You will die on the mountain that you ascend and join your deceased ancestors, just as Aaron your brother died on Mount Hor and joined his deceased ancestors,
NET.51: for both of you rebelled against me among the Israelites at the waters of Meribah Kadesh in the desert of Zin when you did not show me proper respect among the Israelites.
NET.52: You will see the land before you, but you will not enter the land that I am giving to the Israelites.”
